title: Korea Stock Market Today, Oct 12, 2026: KOSPI -3.65%, KOSDAQ -4.83% on French Fiscal Worries
content:
KOSPI closed at 6,384.24, down 3.65%, and KOSDAQ closed at 849.19, down 4.83%, as Korea reopened after the Hangul Day holiday to concerns over French fiscal and political instability, rising U.S. long-term yields and doubts about the durability of AI investment, with heavy foreign selling. Individual themes still moved on their own news: hopes for a southwestern semiconductor cluster and continued hopes for redevelopment of the Seoul Express Bus Terminal.

1. French fiscal worries and U.S. yields — foreign selling drives a sharp drop

Korean markets resumed trading after the Hangul Day holiday and fell sharply as caution toward European financial markets over French fiscal and political instability, higher U.S. long-term yields and worries about how long AI investment can continue all hit at once. France's high budget deficit and public debt and a budget standoff among its politicians pushed government bond yields sharply higher, and the yield gap with German bonds widened, raising concern about fiscal risk in Europe. U.S. long-term yield pressure added to risk aversion across global equities. In Korea, heavy foreign selling hit large chip stocks such as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, which had led the recent rally, and profit-taking spread through growth names including batteries, robotics and chip equipment and materials. KOSPI closed at 6,384.24 (-3.65%) and KOSDAQ at 849.19 (-4.83%).

2. SK chairman and industry minister visit the site — southwestern semiconductor cluster hopes jump

SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won visited the Gwangju military airport site on October 9 to look at the possibility of a southwestern semiconductor cluster, and on October 12 Minister of Trade, Industry and Resources Kim Jung-kwan also visited the site. With the government now visiting rather than only a company reviewing, expectations grew that infrastructure such as industrial complex designation, power, water and roads, and attracting companies could move forward. Seosan, Kumho Electric and Yooshin hit their daily upper limit, and buying spread to Gwangju- and Jeonnam-based construction, civil engineering and infrastructure names including Kumho Engineering & Construction, Dohwa Engineering, Gangdong C&L, Namhwa Civil & Construction and Dasco. Yooshin and Dohwa Engineering are linked to the design and engineering needed for a large industrial complex, Kumho E&C, Namhwa and Dasco to civil works and infrastructure, and Seosan and Kumho Electric to regional ties and development hopes.

3. Seoul Express Bus Terminal redevelopment hopes continue — related stocks stay strong

Hopes for a mixed-use redevelopment of the Seoul Express Bus Terminal continued to lift Dongyang Express, Cheonil Express, Daesung Industrial and Sampyo Cement. Seoul is discussing a plan with the terminal and Shinsegae Central City to move the terminal underground and build a large mixed-use complex above ground, and a redevelopment of a large site in a prime Gangnam location is expected to raise land and stake values. Cheonil Express and Dongyang Express hold stakes in the terminal, which supports hopes of an asset revaluation, and hopes for more demand for cement, ready-mix concrete and other construction materials spread to Sampyo Cement. Because the project is still at the pre-negotiation stage, the price moves reflect long-term hopes and asset revaluation rather than a confirmed schedule.

Quick FAQ

Why did KOSPI and KOSDAQ fall so sharply on Oct 12?
French fiscal and political worries pushed bond yields higher in Europe, U.S. long-term yields and doubts about AI investment added to the caution, and foreign investors sold heavily. KOSPI fell 3.65% and KOSDAQ 4.83%.

Is the southwestern semiconductor cluster confirmed?
No. Interest rose after SK's chairman and the industry minister visited the Gwangju military airport site, but industrial complex designation and company recruitment are still ahead.

How far along is the Seoul Express Bus Terminal redevelopment?
Seoul is in pre-negotiation with Shinsegae Central City and the terminal side on moving the terminal underground and building a mixed-use complex. No development schedule has been confirmed.
